The ISR writes 0 through slot(), which returns &a, so it sets a to 0 as in the model.
STEP 0 assigns the value reached through slot() to c. Since slot() returns &a, this corresponds to the model assignment c=a.

blocks.source_excerpt: STEP(1, { if(c>0) { d=c; bad=(d==0); if(!bad) r=18/d; } });
blocks.correspondence: STEP 1 contains the conditional operations modeled here: when c>0, it copies c to d, sets bad according to whether d is zero, and assigns 18/d to r when bad is false. The whole conditional is one STEP boundary.
